binders: An arbitrary type Omega equipped with a measurable-space structure.
A measure mu on Omega, together with an IsProbabilityMeasure mu instance.
hypotheses: The measure mu satisfies the supplied IsProbabilityMeasure predicate (conventionally, mu is a probability measure).
The exponent satisfies 1 <= p in ENNReal; thus p ranges from 1 through the possible value infinity.
conclusions: The subtype of real-valued almost-everywhere equivalence classes belonging to Lp(p, mu) has at least one NormedAddCommGroup structure.
That same Lp subtype has at least one NormedSpace Real structure.
For every element f of the Lp subtype, its canonical norm is exactly toReal(eLpNorm(cast(f.val), p, mu)).
The universal set in the canonically uniformized Lp subtype is complete, so every Cauchy filter on the whole space converges to an Lp element.
mathematical_definitions: AEEqFun(Omega, Real, mu) is a quotient of real-valued functions by equality almost everywhere with respect to mu.
Lp(Real, p, mu) is the additive subgroup of those almost-everywhere classes f for which eLpNorm(cast(f), p, mu) is strictly below infinity; the target space is its carrier subtype.
eLpNorm is 0 when p = 0, is the essential-supremum norm when p = infinity, and uses the finite-exponent Lp seminorm otherwise.
The canonical norm on the Lp subtype is defined to be the real conversion of the representative's eLpNorm.
IsComplete univ means that every Cauchy filter on the whole canonically uniformized Lp subtype converges to a point of that subtype.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every measurable type Omega, every measure mu carrying the stated probability-measure property, and every extended exponent p with 1 <= p (including p = infinity), the subtype of real-valued almost-everywhere equivalence classes having finite eLpNorm admits a normed additive commutative group structure and a real normed-vector-space structure; its canonical norm is the real value of the eLpNorm of a representative; and the entire resulting canonical uniform space is complete. In standard terminology, the conjunction presents this real Lp space as a Banach space with its canonical Lp norm, while expressing the structural existence, norm formula, and completeness as separate conjuncts.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The statement is restricted to measures satisfying IsProbabilityMeasure, not arbitrary measures.
The value space and scalar field are both Real; no complex- or general-valued Lp space is covered.
The exponent is ENNReal with 1 <= p, so exponents below 1 are excluded and p = infinity is included.
Elements are almost-everywhere equivalence classes represented by a subtype, not literal pointwise functions.

The first two conjuncts assert Nonempty types of structures. They do not bind named structures that later conjuncts use; the norm formula and completeness instead refer to separately inferred canonical Lp instances.
The norm-equality conjunct is definitionally built into MeasureTheory.Lp.instNorm and therefore does not independently constrain an arbitrarily chosen witness of the first Nonempty assertion.
Completeness is stated as IsComplete univ under the inferred canonical uniform structure rather than by returning a CompleteSpace instance.
No contradiction or empty exponent range is apparent: the assumption 1 <= p has ordinary instances such as p = 1, and Lp itself contains at least the zero class.
ambiguities: The packet gives only the type of the inductive predicate MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure and omits its constructors or defining fields. Thus the exact internal meaning of that assumption, including whether it is precisely mu(univ) = 1, is not derivable from this packet alone; the probability interpretation follows the presented identifier and conventional mathematical use.

The packet does not display the internals of the NormedSpace structure or the particular witness of its Nonempty assertion, so the exact scalar-action implementation and its relationship to the later canonical norm instance are not explicit here.

The implementation of ENNReal.toNNReal used inside ENNReal.toReal is outside the dependency boundary. Lp membership forces the eLpNorm being converted to be below infinity, so this omission does not appear to affect the norm formula for actual Lp elements.
